Software Engineering and Information Systems, Master of Science (2 years)
Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering

kuvaus.en:
The master’s degree in Software Engineering and Information Systems offers you a front-row seat to working in the field of information technology. If you want to shape user-centred digital transformation, this programme is for you.

The programme focuses on developing AI and software products, as well as information systems, that are designed around users’ needs.

In your studies, you focus on:

  • software development approaches for new, innovative systems and services,
  • understanding and supporting participatory design, user-centered design, value co-creation, user-driven innovation and human interaction in information technology,
  • how information systems and services can best serve people and organizations in performing personal, knowledge work and other important activities.

The programme will provide the student with relevant, up-to-date skills and capabilities to have a successful future career as a software and ICT expert or manager in a global company or other organisation. We intent to educate advocates of engaging user-centered design interested in innovation, design thinking and building businesses around digital products and services.

The graduating students will have skills to lead multicultural teams, projects and units as well as capabilities to maintain and update their knowledge in the rapidly developing field.

osaamistavoitteet.en:
During your studies, you will gain professional skills as well as relevant theoretical background from the perspectives of software and systems development and current topics, such as digital transformation, artificial intelligence and data analytics.

The skills relevant to working life, such as team and project work, written and oral communication, critical thinking and problem solving, are an essential part of your studies. You will learn the core aspects of the discipline in close cooperation with ICT companies and other organisations.

Minor subjects, such as statistics, mathematics, engineering, management, economics or psychology, are used to complement your studies in your desired application area.

After completing the Master of Science (MSc) degree, you are able to:

  • apply existing and produce new knowledge in Software Engineering or Information Systems to the need of companies and other organisations,
  • act as an independent expert in demanding software or information system projects and manage them professionally,
  • apply the typical research methods and select the most appropriate data collection and analysis methods to solve a specified research problem,
  • develop working methods and practices in their field using a scientific approach, as well as
  • communicate the results clearly and analytically following the scientific practice.

After completing the degree, the student will also achieve the common generic skills of the University of Oulu, which are described on the Common generic skills and learning outcomes of the degrees page.

kuvaus.en: A scholarship is available for the second year’s tuition fee and is based on academic progress.  Please visit the website of University of Oulu for further information.

The scholarship system is meant for non-EU/EEA students who are required to pay tuition fees. Please visit the website of University of Oulu for further information.

teksti.en:
Of the 120 ECTS credits (cr) of the Master of Science degree, 60 cr are common studies to everyone. Those include a research and development project, research methods as well as project and master's seminar. The studies of the chosen orientation are 30 cr, in addition to which the degree includes at least one 10 cr specialisation subject.

The studies of the Software Engineering orientation cover e.g. software production management, artificial intelligence utilisation and software platforms. 

The courses in the Information Systems orientation focus on the utilisation of information technology in organizations and human activities.

The current specialisations are Software Engineering specialisation, Human-Centered Design and User Experience specialisation and Persuasive Design and Gamification specialisation. The specialisations are updated according to the current research areas of the programme's research units.

The scope of the master's thesis is 30 ECTS credits, and its topic is chosen by yourself. It can also be done for either a company or a research project. The thesis work deepens the studies of the chosen orientation and research methods. In the master's phase, the scope of elective studies is 20 cr. They may include either the degree program's own elective studies or minor subject studies.

General work life skills are learned together with the the discipline's own content. Especially analytic and critical thinking, problem solving, continuous learning and application as well as creativity are emphasised in the discipline. Written and oral communication, information retrieval, and teamwork and project skills are an essential part of studies.

The selection between Software Engineering or Information Systems is typically done immediately when the studies begin, and it is confirmed with a personal study plan. It is also possible to begin to study both orientations at the same time and make the final decision during the first semester.

The Software Engineering orientation applies a systematic, disciplined and quantifiable approach to software development in order to obtain reliable and efficient, economically viable software that works as stand-alone application or part of larger information system in an organisation or in an embedded system. The viewpoint of producer and developer of information technology is emphasised in the orientation.

The Information Systems orientation studies the utility and usage of information technology in organisations and various everyday usage situations as well as work practices and effects on human activities. The viewpoint of the exploiter of information technology is emphasised in the orientation.

Because of digitalization and the emerging opportunities of AI, the employment opportunities of graduates of the degree program in Software Engineering and Information Systems are diverse. Internationally, the software market is growing at a rapid pace and expanding into new areas. The development of software and information systems is more international, and more multi-skilled experts of information processing science are required to foster success in the future.


In addition to large companies, especially small companies are driving the growth. In Finland, especially AI applications, cloud computing as well as communication and content applications have been successful. Furthermore, games are also a significant business area.

In the future, the labour market will change due to strengthening digitalisation and automation. Robots will replace many transitional professions, and even more businesses will become software and service oriented. This kind of work requires even more knowledge and skills as well as new ideas.

The graduates from Software Engineering and Information Systems are usually working in ICT companies, service and industrial companies, the public sector and education organisations. In recent years, several graduates have also begun to work for their own companies.

After completing the master’s degree, you are prepared to work in independent, demanding expert roles and manage information systems and software projects. Typical positions for graduates include, for example, project manager, team leader, chief technology officer, chief information officer, software developer, user experience designer, lead developer, full-stack developer, product owner, product manager, data scientist and research coordinator.

The University of Oulu Study Guide for the next academic year will be published in February. Once the Study Guide has been published, you can find the latest degree structure of the programme, including the courses required for the degree, as follows: Go to the Study Guide. Select the upcoming academic year from the academic year menu. Then select the desired level of education (for example, bachelor's programmes, master's programmes, or doctoral programmes), after which you can choose the faculty and programme you are interested in.​

The Master's Thesis that is part of the Master's level studies is usually completed during the fifth study year. After completing the thesis, the student is able to:

  • define relevant focused problem in the field of Software Engineering or Information Systems,
  • apply scientific method as a tool in solving the defined research problem,
  • synthesise research results and evaluate their validity, as well as
  • write a scientific report following a specified format based on the accomplished research.

The Master level studies include also a Maturity Test to show student's familiarity with the field of his or her thesis.

The programme has strong traditions and good experiences in collaboration with companies in information industry. A work-oriented way of completing studies means, for example, that project work is done in cooperation with companies. At the end of both the Master's phases, there is project work integrating studies, commissioned by companies and research organizations. The master's thesis can also be done as an assignment. Thus, student will gain concrete experience on the work tasks of the field and important contacts during their studies.

Working life co-operation is based on the active interaction between research units and companies as well as the public sector. The research in the field is applied by nature and usually carried out empirically in a real world settings. This way education remains up-to-date, and industrial contacts can be invited e.g.as guest lecturers.

In teaching, we co-operate with the local Universities of Applied Sciences. For example, our students can include courses from the degree programmes in Information Processing in Oulu University of Applied Sciences in their degree as optional studies. Co-operation with other universities is carried out internationally.

There are already almost 2000 alumni graduated from the Master's Programme in Software Engineering and Information Systems from the University of Oulu. Their activity is significant both locally, nationally and internationally.

Software engineering and Information systems are a highly international fields, and this is visible also in education. All Master level teaching is in English, and students attending the international Master's programmes take the same courses with Finnish students. Thus, students, who represent over 20 nationalities, gain experience on multi-cultural working environment during their studies. About one third of the staff of the programme's research units are foreigners.

There is a chance to go abroad as an exchange student during studies. There are several options in Nordic countries via Nordplus program, and in Europe via Erasmus exchange program, also many destinations outside Europe are available. During the exchange period, one can choose either courses with similar contents to those offered by the home university or optional studies that are not available at the home university.

University of Oulu provides language studies in Finnish for foreigners, English, Japanese, French, German and Spanish, as well as several other languages are offered as summer courses. Also student tutoring and international responsibilities in student guild and student union offer alternative activities in providing international experience.

The international relations and multinational projects of the programme's research units have a significant effect on education. Students have possibility to accomplish their Master's thesis or Doctoral Dissertation in an international research project. 

The degree programme has also Bachelor Degree Programme in China. It is implemented together with Nanjing Institute of Technology (NJIT). Annually 100 new chinese students begin their studies in the program. NJIT is also one of the exchange destinations where you can study for a bachelor’s degree in English and Chinese.

The teachers and researchers of research groups in the area of Software Engineering and Information Systems provide the teaching of the degree programme. The disciplines of the research groups follow the orientations software engineering and information systems.

Software Engineering (M3S) is the largest software engineering research group in Finland. It carries out scientific research relevant for industry on software development approaches for new innovative systems and services. Its wide network of domestic and international contacts provides a solid basis for empirical research that has high quality academic impact and strong relevance for industry. The emphasis in teaching is in the courses on software engineering.

The Information Systems and Human-Computer Interaction (INTERACT) research group focuses on understanding and supporting participatory design, user-centered design, value co-creation, user driven innovation and human interaction in information technology. The research group acknowledges that information technology has become intertwined and embedded in almost all parts of our everyday life, including leisure and civic activity. The  emphasis in teaching is in the courses on information systems and especially human-computer interaction as well as business aspects.

The Oulu Advanced Research on Services and Information Systems (OASIS) research group studies information systems and service innovation. It focuses on how information systems and services can best serve people and organizations to perform personal, knowledge work and other important activities. Research is in most cases carried out by constructing new concepts and technology and then experimenting with it. We emphasize investigating both the usefulness and the ease of use of such systems and services in parallel. The emphasis in teaching is in the courses on information systems.
The Master's degree (MSc) is a qualification for doctoral studies (PhD) in the same field.

kuvaus.en:
The online application at Studyinfo.fi instructs if you must upload attachments to support your application.​

  • A proof of your English language skills. Applications without the proof of language skills will not proceed in student selection.​
  • The final degree certificate and academic transcript in original language. Official translations of degree certificate and transcript of records are required if they were issued in a language other than Finnish, Swedish, or English.​
  • A copy of passport or identity card if you are not Finnish citizen. If you are not a Finnish citizen but are exempt from paying tuition fees, please note that you must prove this by uploading a document that proves your status as a non-fee-paying applicant.​
  • Preliminary assignment (video)
  • Transcript of Open University studies if you are applying with open university studies based selection

More information regarding admission and language requirements on the website of University of Oulu.
